rows.mensaje: Wait, who proposed continental drift? Please respond to the above in English.
rows.out: Continental drift was first proposed by Alfred Wegener in the early 20th century. He introduced the idea in 1912, suggesting that all continents were once joined together in a single supercontinent, which he called Pangaea, and have since drifted apart. Although his theory was initially met with skepticism, it later gained support with the development of plate tectonics in the 1960s.

rows.mensaje: Largest fish? Please respond to the above in English.
rows.out: The largest fish in the world is the whale shark. Despite its massive size—some individuals can reach up to 40 feet (12 meters) in length—it is a gentle filter feeder and is not dangerous to humans. Whale sharks are found in warm, tropical, and subtropical oceans around the world. They are classified as bony fish (Osteichthyes) and are known for their distinctive, patterned skin. While the oceanic megafauna like blue whales are larger, they are mammals, not fish. So, among true fish, the whale shark holds the title of the largest.

rows.mensaje: Slowest mammal? Please respond to the above in English.
rows.out: The slowest mammal is the three-toed sloth. These mammals move extremely slowly, especially when moving through trees, due to their low metabolic rate and adaptations for life in the canopy of tropical forests. Their slow movement helps conserve energy and avoid predators. While they are not the slowest animals overall (some invertebrates and reptiles move slower), among mammals, the three-toed sloth is widely recognized as the slowest.
